subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with a selected OpenClaw auth profile, should the auth epoch treat the profile credential as canonical identity when present, or should the ambient host/local credential remain part of the session identity?
rationale: Both choices affect auth/session safety: excluding local file presence prevents destructive same-identity resets, but over-broad reuse could cross a real or unprovable credential change.

options.title: Profile credential canonical when present
options.body: Ignore the local Claude CLI fingerprint once a selected auth-profile credential exists, with regression tests for file absent/present, logout, and identity change behavior.

options.title: Host-only Claude CLI policy
options.body: Adopt a backend-level host-only policy like the overlapping PR, after proving it covers this storage-source flip and preserves real host re-login invalidation.

options.title: Keep fail-closed epoch composition
options.body: Keep current local-plus-profile hashing and document that source-presence churn can reset live sessions as an intentional auth safety tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Profile credential canonical when present
recommendation.body: Ignore the local Claude CLI fingerprint once a selected auth-profile credential exists, with regression tests for file absent/present, logout, and identity change behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest feature-history signal for the CLI session auth invalidation behavior and can arbitrate the session/auth boundary with the adjacent owners.
